correctness.rationale: With n=2m the incidence matrix I+S has alternating kernel. Centering also removes the constant mode, giving the stated tangent space and eigenvalues 4 cos^2(pi k/n)/n for its covariance C. Cyclic vertex transitivity makes all squared C-Mahalanobis norms equal to their mean d. Any containing ellipsoid of squared shape Q and center z has tr(Q^-1 C)+||z-c||^2_(Q^-1)<=1. Hence AM-GM gives det Q >= d^d det C with equality only at z=c and Q=dC. The ball similarly minimizes the maximum radius by the mean squared distance identity. Strict convexity excludes nonvertex contacts for both. As an independent determinant check, switch one color class to turn (I+S)(I+S)^T into the ordinary cycle Laplacian. Its nonzero eigenvalues multiply to n times the number n of spanning trees, and restricting to the stated tangent space removes the additional eigenvalue 4. Thus det_H(C)=m^2/n^d. The round-ball ratio is m/2^(m-1), decays strictly from 1 at m=2, and the largest/smallest axes are in the ratio cot(pi/(2m)).
residual_risks: Intrinsic unweighted Euclidean realization only, not a centrally symmetric root polytope or a weighted cycle. Numerical SVD evidence is finite; the rank, optimality, and determinant arguments hold symbolically for all m>=2.

originality.rationale: The covered material is the ordinary even-cycle root polytope, its prior inner geometry, and the general enclosing-ellipsoid/design principle. The supported distinct claim is the explicit outer spectrum and its enclosing-ball-normalized exponential law for this metric realization. Neither same-body inner data nor exact outer ellipsoid results for other edge polytopes give that comparison; the general design result requires the cycle's intrinsic covariance calculation and determinant evaluation.
residual_risks: The source comparison is bounded; an unindexed exact equivalence using affine or augmented optimal design or an alternative name for the polytope remains possible.

value.rationale: The even cycle is a canonical one-parameter test case for intrinsic Euclidean root-polytope geometry. The exact normalized volume loss quantifies, at every size, the failure of the round-ball surrogate even though all vertices are contact points for both outer fits and the axis ratio grows only linearly. This gives explicit outer geometry complementary to the known inner geometry. The value is in that dimension-dependent comparison and exact spectrum, not in recertifying the standard optimal design principle or merely measuring the four-cycle.
residual_risks: The quantitative conclusion is only for this metric family; it is not a new general optimal-design method.
